about: S07.7 (D.23): the monthly parent coaching tips and their Pedagogical Lead review. A tip is delivered only when its status is 'approved' and its review hash matches the exact copy in all three locales (frontend/src/i18n/<locale>/familyGovernance.json, tips.<id>). agent/tools/check-parent-coaching-tips.mjs enforces it and keeps Core's COACHING_TIPS (backend/src/services/parentCoaching.ts) and the client's TIP_IDS equal to this list. To review a tip: read it in three locales, run `node agent/tools/check-parent-coaching-tips.mjs --hash <id>`, set status 'approved' and record review { by, role, at, hash } here and reviewed: true in Core, in one change. docs/operations/PARENT-COACHING.md explains the process.

tips.finding: Paying children for an already-enjoyed activity reduced their later free engagement (Lepper, Greene & Nisbett 1973); practice guidance separates expected family contribution from paid extra work (Lieber 2015).
A stable, legible price for extra work is the design implication of §1.2's contribution-versus-bonus split and §2.4's warning that unexplained rewards read as arbitrary.
Preschoolers who had just met an unreliable adult waited far less on a later delay task (Kidd, Palmeri & Aslin 2013): waiting is rational only where waiting pays.
Parental knowledge that predicts good adjustment comes mostly from the adolescent's own disclosure, and high control is associated with less future disclosure (Stattin & Kerr 2000).
Child-initiated, reciprocal money conversation predicts preparation for financial independence better than parent-to-child delivery (LeBaron, Marks, Rosa & Hill 2020).
What children absorb from how the family handles money day to day often has as strong an impact as deliberate teaching (Gudmunson & Danes 2011).
Effort slows measurably right after a reward is earned before reaccelerating toward the next goal (post-reward resetting, Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng 2006).

The same rules enforced with rationale and voice are internalized; enforced unilaterally, they produce compliance that does not generalize (Joussemet, Landry & Koestner 2008; Soenens & Vansteenkiste 2010).
Gradual separators fare better than early, abrupt ones, and independence granted volitionally predicts better decisions (Beyers, Soenens & Vansteenkiste 2024).
Low delay of gratification can be a rational response to an environment where waiting does not reliably pay off (Kidd et al. 2013); an immediate spend is not by itself a self-control failure.
If Share coins do not visibly go anywhere, the label risks being symbolic rather than operative, compounding the trust risk of §1.3.
Most adults underestimate compound growth, and the bias persists regardless of literacy (Stango & Zinman 2009): a savings bonus should not be presented as teaching compounding.
